title: The start/stop circuit
summary: Turn a momentary Start button into a running motor and stop it again with a normally closed Stop button.
objectives: Explain why Stop uses a normally closed contact

sections.heading: Two buttons, one motor
sections.body: A Start button is **normally open** (TRUE while pressed). A Stop button is **normally closed** (TRUE while not pressed), so a broken wire acts like pressing Stop. The motor may run only while StopPB is TRUE.

sections.heading: Wiring of the panel
sections.body: S1 and S2 go to inputs; the contactor coil K1 to an output.
sections.diagram:
+24V --[S1 NO]--> DI0 (StartPB)
  +24V --[S2 NC]--> DI1 (StopPB)   TRUE while not pressed
  DO0 (MotorContactor) --> K1 coil --> motor M1

sections.heading: Without memory
sections.body: This version only runs while Start is held. Lesson 6 adds memory.

sections.heading: Common mistake
sections.body: Writing `AND NOT StopPB`. Because StopPB is TRUE at rest, `NOT StopPB` is FALSE at rest and the motor would only run while Stop is pressed.

question.question: Nobody touches the Stop button. What is StopPB?
question.explanation: A normally closed contact conducts at rest, so the input is TRUE.

sections.heading: Try the motor station
sections.body: Open the motor station and observe StartPB and StopPB in Variables while you press the buttons.

sections.heading: Summary and troubleshooting note
sections.body:
Start is normally open, Stop is normally closed; Stop must be AND-ed into every run condition.

**Troubleshooting note:** A machine that suddenly will not start after maintenance may have a Stop contact block of the wrong type; check StopPB at rest.

checkpoint.question: Why is a Stop button normally closed?
options: A broken wire then stops the machine
It is required by the PLC

checkpoint.question: Which line is correct for an NC Stop input?
checkpoint.explanation: StopPB is TRUE while Stop is not pressed.
